evals.name: sdk-auth-query-models
evals.prompt: Write Node.js TypeScript code using @shapediver/sdk.platform-api-sdk-v1 to authenticate with a ShapeDiver access key ID and secret, then list my 10 most recent models.
evals.expected_output: A Platform SDK example that creates the SDK client with a Platform root baseUrl, authenticates with passwordGrant using the access key pair, queries client.models.query(...), and reads response.data.result without switching to Geometry Backend code.
assertions: Imports create from @shapediver/sdk.platform-api-sdk-v1.
Passes the Platform root URL as baseUrl rather than /api/v1.
Calls authorization.passwordGrant(accessKeyId, accessKeySecret).
Uses client.models.query(...) for the list request.
Reads models from response.data.result.
Does not use @shapediver/sdk.geometry-api-sdk-v2 or create a Geometry Backend session.

evals.name: rest-oauth-model-get
evals.prompt: Give me cURL commands to authenticate against the ShapeDiver Platform Backend and fetch a model by slug with backend_system, ticket, and backend_ticket embeds.
evals.expected_output: A REST-first answer with an OAuth password-grant request and a protected model GET using the correct Platform endpoints, X-ShapeDiver-Client, and embed parameters, while clearly distinguishing the returned tickets from the Platform bearer token.
assertions: Uses POST {platformRoot}/oauth/token.
Uses the access key ID as username and access key secret as password.
Includes X-ShapeDiver-Client on the protected model request.
Calls GET {platformRoot}/api/v1/models/{slug} or equivalent slug-based model path.
Requests backend_system, ticket, and backend_ticket embeds.
Distinguishes Platform bearer tokens from Geometry Backend tickets.

evals.name: domain-management
evals.prompt: How do I add localhost:3000 and example.com as ShapeDiver embedding domains through the Platform API?
evals.expected_output: A Platform-domain workflow using SDK or REST patterns, exact hostname rules, non-standard port handling, and placeholders for credentials or IDs, without drifting into Viewer or iframe code.
assertions: Uses Platform domain APIs or clearly explains the domain resource workflow.
Mentions exact hostname matching and non-standard port rules.
Warns that subdomains are not implied.
Uses placeholders for credentials and domain values when concrete values are missing.
Does not generate Viewer, App Builder, or Geometry Backend session code.

evals.name: geometry-token-request
evals.prompt: Show TypeScript code to request a Geometry Backend JWT for a ShapeDiver model through the Platform Backend.
evals.expected_output: A Platform SDK example that requests a model token/JWT via modelTokens.create with model ID, scope, and optional lifetime, then explains that the result is for Geometry Backend or Viewer authorization rather than Platform API calls.
assertions: Uses client.modelTokens.create(...) or an explicit Platform token endpoint.
Includes a model identifier plus scope and optional lifetime.
Explains that the returned token is used with the Geometry Backend or Viewer authorization flow.
Does not create a Geometry Backend session or compute outputs.
Distinguishes the JWT from ticket-based access.

evals.name: api-token-create-warning
evals.prompt: I need a ShapeDiver Platform API token for automation. Generate the code and tell me what to watch out for.
evals.expected_output: A Platform SDK or REST example that creates an API token with scope and optional validity metadata, warns that key_secret is only returned once, and treats the resulting secret as sensitive.
assertions: Uses client.apiTokens.create(...) or the REST apitokens endpoint.
Includes scope, description, or validity fields when shown.
Warns that key_secret is returned only once.
Treats the secret as sensitive and does not invent a fake token value.
Stays on the Platform Backend instead of generating Geometry Backend computation code.

evals.name: boundary-run-model
evals.prompt: Use the ShapeDiver Platform Backend to compute outputs and generate an STL export for my model.
evals.expected_output: A boundary-aware answer that explains the Platform Backend can obtain tickets or JWTs but does not run computations, and routes the actual export workflow to the Geometry Backend skill.
assertions: Explains that Platform Backend is for management and authorization, not computation.
Routes output/export execution to shapediver-geometry-backend.
Mentions Platform-issued tickets or JWTs as prerequisites when relevant.
Does not invent Platform-only computation endpoints or SDK methods.
